solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wildly belt more radical party member

indicators.note: something done wildly is done without order, so the following letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: the fifteen letters of these three words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A firebrand activist lashing out with a belt as the most radical member of the party.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal Democrats are a centrist British political party, which makes the radical surface nicely ironic.
explanation.definitionFit: A Liberal Democrat is a member of the UK's Liberal Democrats political party.

clue.text: Young guys protecting European stars

indicators.note: to protect something is to put a guard all round it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: lads are young men
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Young men shielding a European celebrity from the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside LADS: LA(E)DS.
explanation.definitionFit: The leads in a film or play are its principal actors, its stars.

clue.text: Brow rubbed with cloth, being by this?

definitions.text: Brow rubbed with cloth, being by this?

indicators.note: rubbing works material over and around, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sweating worker mops their forehead with a rag while standing next to a hot flame.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: anyone working near this tool would need to wipe their brow.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowtorch produces an intensely hot flame, so standing close to one would make anyone sweat.

clue.text: Fleece or jumper with a bit of khaki?

parts.note: a kangaroo is a jumper

indicators.note: a small bit of a word is a single letter, here its first

parts.note: first letter of khaki

explanation.surface: A shopper choosing between a fleece and a sweater with khaki in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleece and jumper both look like clothing; fleece is the verb to swindle and the jumper is a kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is to cheat or swindle them, which is what fleece means as a verb.

clue.text: A way to punch hooligan and survive

indicators.note: a punch goes into its target, so these letters are driven inside

parts.note: a lout is an uncouth, aggressive young man
taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Advice on fighting off a thug in order to stay alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch' suggests a blow; here it means to pierce, so the short pieces go into the hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: To last out is to endure to the end, so it means survive in the sense of holding on.

clue.text: Old beer in case from Harrods expires

parts.note: ex- means former

indicators.note: in places the beer inside the other letters
the case of a word is its outside, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: outer letters of Harrods
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A crate of old beer bought at a smart London store has passed its date.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrods is a famous London department store. 'Expires' looks like going out of date, but it means breathes out.
explanation.definitionFit: To expire literally means to breathe out, the same action as to exhale.

clue.text: Attentive person in the employ of Eton alumnus?

parts.note: an old boy, a former pupil
a servant is someone employed in another's service

explanation.surface: A watchful footman working for a former pupil of a famous school.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as the old boy's servant. Eton is an English boys' boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Observant means quick to notice things, a close synonym of attentive.

clue.text: Hot under collar after giving a lift to queen with long legs

indicators.note: lifting something takes it out of its place to move it higher up

parts.note: R for Regina, Latin for queen
hot under the collar means cross

explanation.surface: Someone flustered after hoisting up a leggy queen.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, lifting the R in ANGRY moves it to the top: R + ANGY.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangy describes someone tall and slim with long limbs, so having long legs.

clue.text: Somewhat geared to changes, ultimately adaptive

indicators.note: when something changes it is altered, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of adaptive

explanation.surface: A description of someone fairly well set up for change and adaptable in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To a degree is an idiom meaning to some extent, which is what somewhat means.

clue.text: Sexy and glitzy, not ugly essentially

indicators.note: not means without, so the following letters are taken away from the word for glitzy

parts.note: glitzy means showily glamorous

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letters are wanted

parts.note: the two middle letters of the word ugly

explanation.surface: A description of someone attractive and dazzling who, at heart, is anything but plain.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove GL from the front of GLAMOROUS to leave AMOROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorous means showing romantic or sexual desire, so it can stand for sexy in a loose sense.

clue.text: Praise honourable answer hospital enters

indicators.note: something that enters goes inside, so the hospital word sits within the other letters

parts.note: standard abbreviation, as in the Hon. title
A is the abbreviation for answer
short for sanatorium, a hospital for convalescents

explanation.surface: A tribute to an honourable answer given as someone walks into a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: A san, short for sanatorium, is a school or convalescent hospital in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosanna is a shout of praise or adoration to God, used as an exclamation in worship.

clue.text: Place key on seat

indicators.note: on here means added on afterwards, so the key piece is sent second, after the seat piece

parts.note: to seat someone is to sit them down
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave your key on a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seat' looks like a noun but works as the verb, to sit someone down.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location, so it serves as a synonym for place as a noun.

clue.text: Vehicle close to crash with lorry

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters collide and come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A car comes close to crashing into a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as a phrase meaning nearly; in fact close is fodder and 'to crash with' combines it with lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rolls-Royce is a luxury British car, a specific example of a motor vehicle.

clue.text: Sleeping male is surrounded by insects

indicators.note: being surrounded means having things on both sides, so the male sits between the insects

parts.note: a dor is a dung beetle and an ant is another insect
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man sleeping out of doors with bugs crawling all round him.
explanation.walkthrough: The dor, a black dung beetle, is a crossword favourite; the plural insects covers two different ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant means inactive or asleep, as an animal in hibernation lies dormant.

clue.text: Half of France's gloomy, but fit to be leased

parts.note: demi is the French word for half
sable is black, used poetically for gloomy

explanation.surface: A remark that half of France is in a gloomy mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of France' looks like an instruction to take FRAN or NCE; it means the French word for half.
explanation.definitionFit: Demise is a legal term for granting by lease, so a demisable property can be let.

clue.text: Witness where cricket side might play six-footer

parts.note: a national cricket team plays at Test level, in a Test match
an insect has six feet

explanation.surface: A spectator noting where a cricket team might field a very tall player.
explanation.walkthrough: A six-footer sounds like a tall person; here it is an insect with six legs.
explanation.definitionFit: An attestant is one who attests, bearing formal witness to something.

clue.text: Can of cocktail?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for a prison
second meaning: a tequila drink banged on the bar before downing

explanation.walkthrough: Can reads as a tin of ready-mixed drink; it is US slang for jail, and so is the answer, which is also a tequila cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: Slammer is slang for a prison, like can, and a tequila slammer is a well-known mixed drink.

clue.text: Communication system that's a bit dotty?

definitions.text: Communication system that's a bit dotty?

parts.note: surface reading: slightly mad or eccentric
setter's reading: a signalling method literally built of dots and dashes

explanation.walkthrough: Dotty usually means a little crazy; here it means made partly of dots.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse code sends letters as patterns of short and long signals, dots and dashes, by telegraph.

clue.text: Holy man graduates without mortar board?

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the graduates stand on either side

parts.note: two Masters of Arts, MA each
a mortarboard is a flat square academic cap

explanation.surface: A sage among graduates who turned up to the ceremony with no academic cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside: MA(HAT)MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma is an Indian title for a revered sage or saintly person, most famously Gandhi.

clue.text: First-class cases old magistrate deduced

indicators.note: to case something is to enclose it, so the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the digit read as the letter I
a prior was a chief magistrate in medieval Florence and other Italian republics

explanation.surface: A top-quality legal case argued before a magistrate of old.
explanation.walkthrough: The old magistrate is obscure: priors were the chief magistrates of medieval Florence.
explanation.definitionFit: A priori describes reasoning from theory to consequence, so knowledge arrived at by deduction.

clue.text: She might have helped with fertility problems found in A&E

definitions.text: She might have helped with fertility problems

indicators.note: in places the preceding word inside the letters that follow

parts.note: the two letters either side of the ampersand
to found something is to start it

explanation.surface: A doctor in Accident and Emergency who might once have helped couples with fertility problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like a past tense of find; it is the verb to establish. Astarte was a Phoenician goddess of fertility.
explanation.definitionFit: Astarte was the ancient Semitic goddess of fertility and love, so she might have been prayed to for help conceiving.

clue.text: As Racine's plays

indicators.note: plays suggests letters being played around with until they form something new

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A comparison: just like the dramas of the French playwright Racine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' looks like a conjunction but it is the chemical symbol; Racine was a 17th-century French tragedian.
explanation.definitionFit: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic, element number 33.

clue.text: Too much of this and she'll have to stitch up your trousers!

definitions.text: Too much of this and she'll have to stitch up your trousers!

parts.note: surface reading: overindulgence in something, perhaps food

parts.words: she'll have to stitch up your trousers
parts.note: setter's reading: strain on the joins of the trousers calls for the woman who sews for a living

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as SEAM STRESS: too much stress on a seam splits the trousers, and a seamstress repairs them.
explanation.definitionFit: A seamstress is a woman who sews professionally, the person who would mend split trousers.

clue.text: A thing seen behind ship tossing and turning?

parts.note: taken as written
the trail of disturbed water behind a moving vessel

explanation.surface: Something bobbing behind a boat in rough water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tossing and turning' seems to describe the sea; it is a restless sleeper, and the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tossing and turning in bed is not asleep, so they are awake.

clue.text: Aquatic bird seen briefly over mass of ice

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so the letters are read backwards
briefly means cut short, so the bird loses its last letter

parts.note: a grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: A water bird spotted flying over an iceberg.
explanation.walkthrough: GREBE loses its final E to give GREB, which is then reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A berg is short for iceberg, a large floating mass of ice.

clue.text: Caller made a speculation on radio

indicators.note: on the radio you hear words, not see them, so the sound is what matters

parts.note: made a speculation means guessed

explanation.surface: A radio phone-in caller ventured a wild guess on air.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest is a visitor, someone who calls at your home.

clue.text: He might do sailor's knots and I might draw

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who ties knots
second meaning: one who ties a game, drawing it

explanation.walkthrough: Draw reads as making a picture, but a draw is a tie, so both halves describe someone who ties.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is literally one who ties, whether knotting rope or finishing level in a match.

clue.text: Swag stuffed aboard transports close to Kiev

indicators.note: something stuffed has another thing packed inside it
to transport is to move things about, so the letters are carried into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: last letter of Kiev

explanation.surface: Loot packed on board vehicles heading for the Ukrainian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swag' looks like loot, but here it is short for swagger.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is boastful, swaggering show of boldness, and swag is informal for that kind of swagger.

clue.text: Smelly old dons hit yours truly after beginning of seminar

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the old letter is worn inside the other pieces

parts.note: a hit record is a No. 1, read as letters

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: first letter of seminar
O is the abbreviation for old
the setter referring to themself

explanation.surface: Elderly academics striking the setter at the start of a stuffy seminar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like university tutors, but it is the verb: O goes into NO1-S-ME, with the digit 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or disgusting, especially of a smell, so it fits smelly.

clue.text: I turn and circle Crete at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor describes turning and circling round the island of Crete.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word looks like the speaker; it is the physics symbol I for electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics equations the symbol I stands for current, the flow of electric charge.
